description: Assesses the appropriate cost management and sustainability strategy based on budget constraints, service type, traffic profile, and deployment model.

recommendation.rationale: Workloads with spiky or unpredictable traffic benefit from pay-per-use pricing models that scale costs with actual demand. This avoids paying for idle capacity during quiet periods while ensuring resources are available during peaks. Serverless and auto-scaling services align cost directly with value delivered.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: No dedicated FinOps role needed; cost scales automatically with usage
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Cost anomaly monitoring, budget threshold reviews, and periodic optimisation reviews

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Highly variable; directly proportional to usage; zero cost at zero traffic
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Application architecture changes to support serverless/auto-scaling patterns

recommendation.rationale: Workloads with steady, predictable traffic benefit from reserved capacity or savings plans that provide significant discounts (30-70%) in exchange for commitment. The predictable nature of the workload makes commitment-based pricing low-risk and high-value.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires periodic review of commitment utilisation; finance team involvement for budget planning
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Quarterly commitment reviews, utilisation monitoring, and renewal planning

costConsiderations.runningCosts: 30-70% lower than on-demand for committed resources; predictable monthly costs
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Upfront commitment (partial or full); analysis effort to right-size commitments

recommendation.rationale: Budget-constrained small teams should prioritise managed services that eliminate infrastructure management overhead. While per-unit costs may be higher, the total cost of ownership is lower when accounting for reduced staffing needs and operational burden.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Minimal operational overhead; team focuses on application development rather than infrastructure
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Cost monitoring and periodic service tier reviews

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low for small-scale services; free tiers available for many managed services
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Minimal; managed services reduce setup complexity

recommendation.rationale: Data platforms with growing data volumes require tiered storage strategies that automatically move data to cheaper storage tiers as it ages. This prevents storage costs from growing linearly with data volume while maintaining access to recent data at full performance.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard team can configure lifecycle policies; no dedicated storage team needed
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Lifecycle policy reviews, storage cost monitoring, and data classification updates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Significantly reduced compared to single-tier storage; 60-90% savings on archived data
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Lifecycle policy configuration; data classification exercise

recommendation.rationale: Without cloud access, cost management focuses on infrastructure consolidation, virtualisation efficiency, and lifecycle planning. The primary optimisation levers are reducing hardware footprint through consolidation and extending useful life through proper maintenance.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires capacity planning skills; finance team involvement for hardware lifecycle budgeting
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Capacity reviews, hardware refresh planning, consolidation opportunities, and power efficiency monitoring

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Fixed costs (hardware, power, cooling, licensing); less variable than cloud
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Capacity planning tools; consolidation effort; potential hardware refresh

defaultRecommendation.pattern: Cloud Cost Governance with Tagging and Budgets
defaultRecommendation.rationale: When no specific conditions strongly favour an alternative, implementing cloud cost governance with resource tagging, budget alerts, and regular cost reviews provides visibility and control. This foundation enables informed decisions about further optimisation.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Any team member can monitor costs; no specialist FinOps role needed initially
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Monthly cost reviews and budget threshold updates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Cost management tools are typically free or low-cost

commonQuestions: What is the budget for this service?
Is there a preference for CapEx or OpEx spending?
What is the expected growth rate of the service?
Are there existing cloud commitments or enterprise agreements?
Who is responsible for cost management?
Are there sustainability targets for the organisation?
evidenceNeeded: Expected traffic and data growth projections
